provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Water in our environment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list sources of water.
The pupils should be able to differentiate between clean and dirty water.
Introduction:
We use water every day like when we drink or wash.
Today we will learn about water around us.
Content:
Sources of water are rain, rivers, wells, and boreholes. Water in the river is from rain. We get water from the tap in our school. Some people fetch water from the well.
Clean water is clear and has no dirt. Dirty water has germs and can make us sick. We should not drink dirty water from the roadside.
Class activity:
Bring samples of clean and dirty water. Let pupils look and smell them. Ask them to say which one is safe to drink.
Evaluation questions:
Where do we get water from?
What is the difference between clean and dirty water?
Why should we not drink dirty water?
Summary:
Water comes from different places and we must use clean water to stay healthy.

topics.title: Uses of water
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the uses of water.
The pupils should be able to explain how to save water.
Introduction:
We drink water every day to stay alive.
Water is very useful in many ways.
Content:
We use water for drinking, cooking, washing, and farming. When we are thirsty we drink water. Our mothers use water to cook rice. We use water to wash our bodies and clothes.
We should save water by turning off the tap after use. We can use the same water to water plants. Do not play with water to waste it.
Class activity:
Let pupils draw one way they use water at home. They will show the class and explain what they drew.
Evaluation questions:
What do we use water for?
How can we save water at home?
Why should we not waste water?
Summary:
Water is useful for many things and we must not waste it.

topics.title: Air in our environment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state that air is everywhere.
The pupils should be able to explain how moving air does work.
Introduction:
We breathe air every day without seeing it.
Today we will learn about air around us.
Content:
Air is all around us. We cannot see air but we feel it when it blows. Air is in the classroom, outside, and even in water.
Moving air can do work. The wind blows the leaves on trees. We use moving air to dry our clothes. A fan moves air to cool us.
Class activity:
Let pupils blow air on their hands to feel it. They will wave a paper to see how air moves it.
Evaluation questions:
Where can we find air?
What does moving air do?
How do we use air in our daily life?
Summary:
Air is everywhere and moving air can help us do work.

topics.title: The weather instruments
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify a rain gauge and wind vane.
The pupils should be able to state how to observe the weather.
Introduction:
The weather changes every day like when it rains or the sun shines.
We use special tools to measure weather.
Content:
A rain gauge measures how much rain falls. It has a container to collect rain water. A wind vane shows which way the wind blows. It has an arrow that points to the wind direction.
We can observe the weather by looking at the sky. If the sky is dark it might rain. If the sky is clear the sun will shine.
Class activity:
Show pupils pictures of rain gauge and wind vane. Let them draw one of the instruments and label its parts.
Evaluation questions:
What is a rain gauge used for?
What does a wind vane show?
How do we know if it will rain?
Summary:
We use rain gauge and wind vane to measure weather changes.

topics.title: The water cycle
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how rain forms.
The pupils should be able to draw a simple water cycle.
Introduction:
Rain comes from the sky and goes to rivers and seas.
Today we will learn how water moves in a cycle.
Content:
The sun heats water in rivers and seas. The water turns to vapor and goes up. When the vapor cools it becomes rain. Rain falls on the land and flows back to rivers.
We can draw the water cycle by showing the sun, water vapor, rain, and rivers. The water keeps moving in this cycle all the time.
Class activity:
Let pupils draw the water cycle in their notebooks. They will use arrows to show how water moves.
Evaluation questions:
How does rain form?
What happens to water when the sun heats it?
Draw a simple water cycle.
Summary:
Water moves in a cycle from earth to sky and back again.

topics.title: Soil types
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify sand, loam and clay soil.
The pupils should be able to compare different soil types.
Introduction:
Soil is what plants grow in like beans in our school farm.
Today we will learn about different kinds of soil.
Content:
Sand soil has tiny grains that feel rough. Water flows through sand quickly. Loam soil is dark and soft. It is good for growing plants. Clay soil feels smooth when wet. It holds water very well.
We can feel the soil with our hands. Sand feels gritty, loam feels crumbly, and clay feels sticky when wet.
Class activity:
Give pupils samples of sand, loam and clay. Let them feel each soil and say how it feels.
Evaluation questions:
What does sand soil feel like?
Which soil is good for growing plants?
How is clay soil different from sand soil?
Summary:
There are different types of soil and each has special qualities.

topics.title: Things made from soil
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list things made from soil.
The pupils should be able to explain how pots are made.
Introduction:
We use clay to make pots in our local market.
Soil can be made into many useful things.
Content:
We make pots, bricks, and plates from soil. Pots are made from clay soil. The clay is mixed with water and shaped. Then it is dried in the sun. Bricks are made from soil and used to build houses.
We can make small pots by rolling clay into a ball and making a hole in the middle. We let it dry in the sun for many days.
Class activity:
Let pupils make small clay pots using clay soil. They will shape it and let it dry.
Evaluation questions:
What things can we make from soil?
How do we make pots from clay?
What are bricks used for?
Summary:
Soil is used to make pots, bricks and other useful things.

topics.title: Reproduction in plants
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state that seeds grow into plants.
The pupils should be able to explain how bean seeds sprout.
Introduction:
We planted beans in our school garden last week.
Today we will learn how plants grow from seeds.
Content:
Plants grow from seeds. A seed has a baby plant inside. When we plant a seed in soil with water, it grows roots and then a stem. The stem grows up and leaves come out.\Bean seeds are good for sprouting. We put bean seeds in wet cotton. After two days, a small root comes out. Then a stem grows up with leaves.
Class activity:
Let pupils plant bean seeds in wet cotton. They will watch it grow for one week and draw what they see each day.
Evaluation questions:
What do seeds need to grow?
How long does it take for a bean seed to sprout?
Draw a bean seed that has started to grow.
Summary:
Seeds grow into plants when they have water and soil.

topics.title: Reproduction in animals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state that animals have babies.
The pupils should be able to match parent animals to their young.
Introduction:
We saw a mother dog with puppies last week.
Today we will learn how animals have babies.
Content:
Animals make babies to continue their kind. Some animals lay eggs like chickens and snakes. Other animals give birth to live babies like cats and dogs.
The baby of a cow is called a calf. The baby of a goat is called a kid. The baby of a chicken is called a chick.
Class activity:
Show pupils pictures of parent animals and their young. Let them match each parent to its baby.
Evaluation questions:
What do we call the baby of a cow?
How do chickens have babies?
Match the mother goat to her baby.
Summary:
Animals have babies in different ways like laying eggs or giving birth.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions about term's work.
The pupils should be able to participate in class quiz.
Introduction:
We have learned many things this term about water, air, soil and plants.
Today we will revise all we have learned.
Content:
We will talk about water, air, soil types, and how plants and animals reproduce. We will remember the uses of water and the water cycle. We will also talk about weather instruments and things made from soil.
We will play a quiz game. The teacher will ask questions and pupils will raise hands to answer. Pupils who answer correctly will get points.
Class activity:
Divide the class into two teams. Ask questions about what we learned this term. The team with more points wins.
Evaluation questions:
Name two sources of water.
What does a wind vane show?
How do plants grow from seeds?
Summary:
We have revised all we learned this term and we are ready for the exam.
